position: Retention is classified here and decided nowhere. Each family below has a governance class, a default the design would run on, a ceiling and a clock -- and a decision reference for the period an operator still owes. Nothing in this repository enforces any of them: there is no audit schema, no migration, no job and no reader. These cases pin the classification and pin the fact that it is not yet enforcement.

families.name: access audit -- hot tier, full fields
access to a restricted class
families.doc_default_text: never tiered below actor-pseudonym + object id
families.ceiling: 1 y, extendable only by a hold

families.doc_default_text: **14 d**, or the close of the gate window that cites them

families.default_horizon: 30 d and 5,000 rows and 16 MiB, whichever binds first

families.default_horizon: until the gate decision they inform is recorded, + 90 d
families.doc_default_text: until the gate decision they inform is recorded, + 90 d

families.doc_default_text: until the incident is closed and released by the custodian

refusal quarantine class: R0-derived as coded, or R4-audit as the API contract table says (finding RT-1)

fail-open versus fail-closed on audit-store unavailability

undecided_decisions.default: documented non-erasure, because the encryption crypto-shredding requires does not exist

undecided_decisions.default: not guessed; set from a week of stage-0 logs

rt1_finding.statement: docs/phase6-operator-api-contract.md maps enforce_refusal_retention() to R4-audit (1 y); the function defaults to 30 days and raises above 90, citing the R0-derived ceiling. One of the two is wrong and the retention design says the code is right.

row_state_cases.name: a-pruned-row-at-the-shared-horizon-is-not-loss
row_state_cases.why: A TTL that fired between the two reads is correct behaviour on both sides.

row_state_cases.name: a-prune-far-from-any-horizon-is-a-finding
row_state_cases.why: Reported and triaged, never gate-blocking: a horizon disagreement is a policy defect, not a data loss proof.

no_enforcement_yet.why: The retention design creates no table, no migration, no route, no credential and no bucket. A test that lets one appear quietly would make the design's own claim untestable.
